articles.title: These Researchers Made AI Drive a Toyota Corolla to Get In-N-Out
articles.summary: Three engineers put GPT, Claude, and Grok in charge of a real car. Only one of them was successful.
articles.paragraph: Three engineers put GPT, Claude, and Grok in charge of a real car. Only one of them was successful. LoaderSave StorySave this storyCommentLoaderSave StorySave this storyAditya Ramabadran, Simon Mahns, and Tobias Gessler, three AI engineers at a startup called Axiom, recently fancied In-N-Out Burger for lunch. They weren’t about to drive themselves, though. Sitting in a 2024 Toyota Corolla near the Bay Area restaurant’s drive-thru lane, they opened a laptop and asked OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra to take the wheel. They linked a chat interface to a server, which was connected to several windscreen-mounted cameras and the car’s power steering system. A safety driver kept one foot above the brake, just in case.

articles.title: ChatGPT is getting a lot more visual, with the launch of a new interface
articles.summary: OpenAI is launching a new user interface that will bring interactive visuals to ChatGPT.
articles.paragraph: OpenAI is launching a new user interface that will bring interactive visuals to ChatGPT. AI ChatGPT is getting a lot more visual, with the launch of a new interface Lucas Ropek 11:00 AM PDT · October 7, 2026 ChatGPT is about to get a lot more visual, thanks to a new feature that OpenAI calls Intelligent UI. The new interface, which is being rolled out Wednesday with a new GPT-6 model, will integrate a significant amount of visuals into users’ conversations. OpenAI says many of those visuals will be interactive. In other words, instead of just flat, cartoonish pictures, the chatbot will frequently include things like tappable buttons, a customized calculator for a specific task, interactive charts, editable graphs, and other elements the user can work with directly.

articles.title: The New ChatGPT Is More Show Than Tell
articles.summary: OpenAI is updating ChatGPT for all users with an “Intelligent UI” that’s more visual—generating interactive elements as part of the chatbot’s outputs.
articles.paragraph: OpenAI is updating ChatGPT for all users with an “Intelligent UI” that’s more visual—generating interactive elements as part of the chatbot’s outputs. LoaderSave StorySave this storyCommentLoaderSave StorySave this storyWhen you ask a chatbot a question, you’ll often get a wall of text back, maybe with an image or two pulled from the web. That may no longer be the case soon, as OpenAI overhauls how ChatGPT answers prompts. On Wednesday, OpenAI unveiled an “Intelligent UI” update for ChatGPT that generates visual, custom elements—when helpful—for answering a user's questions. The company's new experience is powered by its recent GPT-6 model, which rolls out to paid users today and to free users tomorrow.

articles.title: Netgear reveals new dark web monitoring tool which will tell you if your personal data turns up online
articles.summary: Netgear’s new Dark Web Monitoring service can alert users as soon as personal data is found on the dark web.
articles.paragraph: Shine a light on your data The dark web is the hidden arena of the internet where various “out of sight” transactions are conducted. While it has legitimate uses (such as dissidents accessing resources via Tor), it is also the home of a black market in data – typically stolen from large organizations, companies, and governments in successful hacking attempts. Owners of the data should be notified by law when their information is stolen. However, often it isn’t until personal information (and more valuable data such as company secrets or software engines) hits the dark web that companies are even aware that they have been hacked. This makes dark web monitoring services such as Netgear’s new feature particularly attractive.

articles.title: Surface Laptop Ultra hands-on: A beautiful beast powered by NVIDIA's RTX Spark
articles.summary: Yes, it's just a premium laptop. But it sure looks pretty.
articles.paragraph: Yes, it Devindra Hardawar for Engadget Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover When we first caught a glimpse of the Surface Laptop Ultra back in June, I was struck by how normal it seemed. Even though Microsoft claimed it was the most powerful Surface Laptop ever, it really looked like a straightforward MacBook Pro clone, even more so than the Surface Laptop (or the Laptop Studio, which nobody talks about anymore). There aren't any weird hinges or flashy Surface features — just pure premium laptop by the looks of it. After spending a bit of time with it today, I can confirm that remains the case. At the same time, it feels better than any other Windows laptop I've held before. And given its $2,599 starting price, it damn well better be.

articles.title: The internal chemistry of phytoplankton changes as oceans become more acidic
articles.summary: Our oceans are becoming more acidic, which could have major consequences for marine life. Of particular concern is what this could mean for phytoplankton, the microscopic photosynthetic organisms that...
articles.paragraph: Our oceans are becoming more acidic, which could have major consequences for marine life. Of particular concern is what this could mean for phytoplankton, the microscopic photosynthetic organisms that form the basis of marine food webs and produce roughly half of the oxygen on Earth. Now, a study published in Nature Geoscience has found that the carbon dioxide we pump into the atmosphere is changing their internal chemistry.
